## Proof

**Key identification.** For a smooth function $f: M \to \mathbb{R}$, the pushforward $(f_*)_p: T_p M \to T_{f(p)}\mathbb{R}$ is a linear map. Since $T_{f(p)}\mathbb{R}$ is canonically isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}$ (via the coordinate $t$ on $\mathbb{R}$), under this identification we have
$$
(f_*)_p(v_p) \;=\; v_p(f)\,\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{f(p)},
$$
so $(f_*)_p(v_p) = (f_*)_p(w_p)$ is equivalent to
$$
v_p(f) = w_p(f) \qquad (\star)
$$
for every smooth $f: M \to \mathbb{R}$.

**Tangent vectors are derivations.** Recall that a tangent vector $v_p \in T_p M$ is a derivation at $p$: a linear map $v_p: C^\infty(M) \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the Leibniz rule $v_p(fg) = v_p(f)\,g(p) + f(p)\,v_p(g)$. Two derivations are equal if and only if they agree on every smooth function. Condition $(\star)$ says precisely that $v_p$ and $w_p$ agree on every $f \in C^\infty(M)$, so as derivations $v_p = w_p$.

**Concrete verification via coordinates (optional rigor).** To make this fully explicit: choose a chart $(U, \varphi = (x^1, \dots, x^n))$ centered at $p$. For each $i$, extend the coordinate function $x^i$ (defined on $U$) to a global smooth function $\tilde{x}^i \in C^\infty(M)$ using a smooth bump function that equals $1$ in a neighborhood of $p$. Applying $(\star)$ to $f = \tilde{x}^i$ gives
$$
v_p(\tilde{x}^i) = w_p(\tilde{x}^i).
$$
Since $\tilde{x}^i = x^i$ near $p$, and derivations at $p$ depend only on the germ of a function, $v_p(\tilde{x}^i) = v_p(x^i)$ and likewise for $w_p$. Hence
$$
v_p(x^i) = w_p(x^i) \quad \text{for all } i = 1, \dots, n.
$$
Writing both vectors in the coordinate basis,
$$
v_p = \sum_{i=1}^n v_p(x^i)\,\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\right|_p, \qquad
w_p = \sum_{i=1}^n w_p(x^i)\,\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\right|_p,
$$
the components coincide, so $v_p = w_p$. $\blacksquare$
